clearAnchor.where: Beside the input box for a new note
clearAnchor.what: Detach this note from its section so it applies to the document as a whole.

todoStatus.what: Left-click cycles the status, right-click toggles "skipped".
todoStatus.name: Click to cycle status; right-click to toggle skipped

s6.title: Plan window
s6.p1: The toolbar above a plan document. Everything here is a symbol; not one is an image file. As the window narrows the buttons fold right to left into the ⋯ menu — Todos goes first, Approve last — so the same document shows a different number of buttons at different widths.
s6.note: The progress bar under the badge uses the same palette, so the two are always consistent.

history.name: History (📜 on the rail)
history.what: Read back through past agent conversations.

tokens.name: Tokens (📊 on the rail)
tokens.what: Token usage statistics. The small number beside this icon on the rail is the running total.

schedule.name: Schedule (🗓 on the rail)
schedule.what: Scheduled tasks. The interface says Schedule, not Tasker.

messages.name: Messages (✉ on the rail)
messages.what: The record of cross-pane messages sent and received.

preview.name: Preview (👁 on the rail)
preview.what: File preview and the change record track.

collapse.where: End of the expanded tab strip
collapse.what: Collapse the whole rail back. Any icon on the rail then expands it and switches to that tab.
collapse.name: Collapse panel

resetCounters.where: One on each of the three statistics blocks in the Tokens tab
resetCounters.what: Zero that scope's statistics. The three have different scopes: this run, this workspace, global. It asks first.

s7.title: Right rail and Messages
s7.p1: The same set of tabs has two looks: collapsed to a rail they are emoji, expanded the tab strip uses line icons. Both columns are shown side by side.

callout.title: This area has no icons
callout.text: Every button in the Messages panel is a text button; there is no symbol or icon to match against. Go by the wording instead:

pauseResume.effect: Pause or resume message delivery as a whole. While paused, messages queue instead of reaching panes.

clearLog.effect: Clear this log's display (delivered messages are unaffected).

withdraw.where: On a message row that is still queued
withdraw.effect: Withdraw this message. It only works before delivery. The tooltip is Take this message back before it reaches the target pane.

resend.where: On a message row that failed or was withdrawn

idle.meaning: Open but with nothing to do.
idle.advice: Go ahead and give it an instruction.

awaiting.meaning: The CLI asked you something and is stuck waiting for an answer. The moving style exists precisely so it does not look like "nothing is happening".

waiting.meaning: A placeholder row that has not actually started.
waiting.advice: Click it to bring it up.

stopped.advice: A disconnection can be recovered from the status bar's ⚡.

awaiting.tooltip: Needs you — an agent in this group is blocked on a permission or a question / A CLI in this tab is waiting on you

active.tooltip: Running — an agent in this group is active / Some CLIs in this tab are running

idle.tooltip: Idle — agents are open, none running / Every CLI in this tab is idle

empty.tooltip: Not opened — every pane here is waiting to be restored / This tab has no panes

autoNamed.where: Right of the name, in the pane title and on the sidebar pane row
autoNamed.meaning: This name was picked automatically from the first instruction of this session. Rename it by hand and the mark is gone for good.
autoNamed.name: Named automatically from this session's first instruction — rename it and it stays yours

manager.name: Global Manager / Stage manager, shown as 🎯 Mgr
manager.where: The pane title and the sidebar pane row
manager.meaning: This pane is the pipeline's stage manager, deciding when each stage ends.

expand.name: (no tooltip)
expand.where: Right side of the sidebar pane row
expand.meaning: More information can be expanded. Once expanded it turns 90 degrees to point down. This is not the same thing as the plan window's ▶ Execute.

s8.title: Status colors and marks
s8.h1: The dot on a pane row (in front of every pane row in the sidebar)
s8.h2: The square on group rows and tabs
s8.p1: These are not buttons, but they are what users ask about most: "what does this colored dot mean?"
s8.p2: A circle, 8px. The colors can be customized in Settings; the table below is the factory default.
s8.p3: A 7px rounded square, deliberately a different shape from the dot above, because it speaks for a whole group rather than one pane. The sidebar group row and the tab bar follow the same rule and the same colours, in four states; amber outranks green — one pane waiting on you paints the whole group amber even while its neighbours are still running. Both squares also follow the palette you set in the Status badges page:

callout.title: Three states, not two
callout.text: Green and blue are the two "there is something in here" states; gray is the third — nothing in this group has actually started yet (or there are no panes at all). A gray dot does not mean something is broken.

s8.h4: The count pill on a workspace heading
s8.p4: The number pill to the right of a workspace name is itself a status light. It uses the pane-status palette from the first table above (and honours the same Status badges override), and its colour names the one pane under that heading that most wants you. The order is "what is stuck on me", not "what is worst": awaiting → error → running → starting → idle → disconnected → stopped → exited → waiting. Hovering spells the status out.

callout2.title: The group row’s number is grey on purpose
callout2.text: The same pill stays colourless on a group row, because that row already says its run state in the square beside the name. The square has four states and a pane status has nine; two different scales side by side just read as two signals disagreeing. A workspace heading has no square, and it is often the only row left on screen once its section is folded — so it is the one that gets the colour.

icons.intro: A lookup table for button icons: spot a button in the interface and come here for its name, which area it lives in, and what pressing it does. Every one of them matches an icon that really exists in the code, and the name column keeps the original English title / aria-label.

howto.title: How to use this table
howto.text: Work out which area the button on screen belongs to, turn to that chapter, and match the shape in the "Icon" column. The name column is the original tooltip string that floats up on hover — when two shapes look alike, rest the pointer on the button for a second and the text that appears matches this column directly.

locator.caption: Which part of the main window belongs to which chapter. The numbers on the picture are the chapter numbers — spot a button, work out which region it sits in, then turn to that chapter. Chapter 5 (Git pane) and chapter 6 (Plan window) are separate surfaces and are not in this picture; chapter 8 is about colour, and its tables draw the real dots.

sidebar.label: Chapter 1 · Sidebar
sidebar.text: The tab icons across the top, and the workspace → group → pane list below them.

panes.label: Chapter 2 · The pane itself
panes.text: A pane's title bar and its buttons: rebuild, minimise, the ∞ loop, the quota badge.

tabs.label: Chapter 3 · Stage and tab bar
tabs.text: The tab bar itself, plus the four arrangement modes and the grid ratio toolbar at its right end.

status.label: Chapter 4 · Status bar
status.text: Environment state on the left (branch, backend, resources); whatever is in progress on the right.

rail.label: Chapter 7 · Right rail and Messages
rail.text: The right-hand panel collapsed to a rail: History, Tokens, Schedule, Messages, Preview.

s9.title: Prompt skill icons
s9.p1: Every prompt skill carries its own icon, and it shows up in three places: the slots of the skill ring that fans out of the title bar’s ∞ button, the heading of the preview card beside that ring, and the editing drawer in Settings ▸ Prompts. These 24 are the built-in vector icons, drawn from the same shapes the product uses.
s9.useCol: What it draws, and what it suits
s9.p2: To use something else, type a character or paste an emoji into the last box of the icon row. Only the first character is kept (a ZWJ emoji sequence or a flag counts as one) — paste a whole string and the rest is dropped, because a ring slot has room for exactly one glyph.

advance.what: Fast-forward — work that keeps pushing ahead.

green.what: Check in a circle — verify, get the suite to green.

doc.what: Page with a folded corner — docs and reports.

refactor.what: Cycle arrow — refactor and tidy in rounds.

edit.what: Pencil — a one-off prompt written on the spot.

bug.what: Beetle — hunt and fix a defect.

rocket.what: Rocket — ship it, cut a release.

sparkle.what: Two sparks — clean up and polish.

terminal.what: Prompt — run something in a shell.

eye.what: Eye — review and watch without touching.

star.what: Star — the one that matters most.

crossPlatform.intro: Navide runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, but the other seven topics all describe the macOS window. This page covers only what genuinely differs between the three: which file to download, how updating works, which buttons moved, and what the platform-specific machinery underneath means for you in practice. Anything not mentioned here behaves as the other topics describe.

s1.title: Getting it and installing it
s1.p1: Every release ships macOS, Windows and Linux installers at the same time. Take the one for your platform.

macos.how: Drag it to Applications and open it normally. It is signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple, so no Gatekeeper workaround is needed. Requires macOS 13 or newer on Apple silicon.

winX64.how: For the usual Intel or AMD machine.

winArm.how: For an Arm-based Windows machine. This is a native build, not x64 under emulation.

linuxAppImage.how: chmod +x it, then run it. It carries its own FUSE runtime, so no libfuse package is needed.

linuxDeb.how: Install it with sudo apt install. It lands in /opt/Navide/navide, puts a navide command on PATH, and adds a desktop entry.

s1.note: Each release also carries a .zip and a few .yml manifests. Those are what the in-app updater reads; installing by hand needs only one of the five files above.
s1.p2: It is not a one-click installer: it asks which directory to install into, and it installs for the current Windows user rather than for the whole machine, so it needs no administrator rights. The shortcut it creates is called Navide.

callout.title: SmartScreen blocks the first run
callout.text: The Windows installer is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC" with the publisher listed as unknown. Choose More info, then Run anyway. Every new installer asks again; it is not a sign that the download was tampered with.

s1.p3: macOS ships for Apple silicon only — there is no Intel build. Linux ships x64 only; an arm64 build exists but is produced solely on a manual build run and is not published yet.

s2.title: Where downloads come from: GitHub and dl.navide.dev
s2.p1: The same file is served from two places: Navide's own download mirror at dl.navide.dev, and GitHub Releases. The mirror is the primary source and GitHub is the fallback; both carry the same bytes, not two different builds.

list.readme: The README's download list carries a mirror link beside every line, pointing at the same file on the mirror. Whichever side is slow for you, take the other.
list.identical: The two are byte for byte identical. After writing the mirror, the release pipeline downloads every file back from dl.navide.dev and compares sha256 sums, failing the step on any mismatch — so the mirror is never stale and never half-uploaded.
list.website: The website and the README download lists both link to the mirror directly, with the GitHub link beside it.

s2.p2: Updating reads the mirror by default: the app sets its update feed to dl.navide.dev at startup. It falls back to GitHub only on a network-level failure — host not found, connection refused, timeout, a 5xx or 429 from the server — and once it has fallen back it stays on GitHub for the rest of that run. There is no path back to the mirror; a restart begins from the mirror again.
s2.note: A 404 or a checksum mismatch does not trigger the fallback. Both hosts hold the same file, so switching would fail the same way; reporting the error as-is is what makes the real problem visible.

s3.title: Auto-update across platforms
s3.p1: In-app updating is not available for every way of installing. What decides it is the install shape, not the operating system.

win.updates: Yes — but because the installer is not code-signed, updates are installed without signature verification for the same reason.

deb.updates: No. Updates for that install come from apt, alongside the rest of the system's packages.

s3.h1: The three stages behave identically everywhere
s3.p2: Settings ▸ Updates splits updating into Check, Download and Install, and none of the three changes with the platform: automatic checks are on by default, automatic download is on by default but applies only to patch releases, and install-on-quit is off by default. Installing always restarts the app, and every CLI pane with it — which is exactly what the button says: "Restart to install".

callout.title: What that page looks like on a .deb install
callout.text: The Check for updates button is disabled, the status line reads "Automatic updates aren't available in this build.", and the three-stage track is blank. Nothing is broken — that install shape hands updating to the package manager by design.

s4.title: Differences you will actually notice
s4.h1: Window controls and the menu bar
s4.p1: Navide draws its own title bar. On macOS the system still paints the traffic lights over it; on Windows and Linux it does not — a frameless window on Linux genuinely has no buttons at all — so on those two platforms Navide draws its own minimize, maximize/restore and close buttons at the top right.

list.controls: Those three buttons always sit above everything else, including the welcome screen you see before any project is open. No overlay can cover them.
list.menubar: On Windows and Linux the native menu bar is hidden by default — press Alt to reveal it — so it does not stack a second bar on top of the drawn title bar.
list.appMenu: Neither platform has the macOS application menu, so Settings…, Check for Updates… and Quit live under File instead.
list.closeItem: The Window menu gains a Close item for closing the window. macOS has no such item, because there ⌘W is reserved for closing a pane.
list.pluginWindows: Windows drawn by a Navide plugin — the Git window among them — use the system's own frame on Windows and Linux rather than the drawn controls: what runs inside them is the Navide plugin's own content, which has no bridge to the host and so cannot draw the buttons itself.

s4.h2: Closing the last window asks first
s4.p2: On Windows and Linux, closing the last window quits the whole application. So Navide asks before the window actually closes, which is the only moment Cancel can still do anything — asked afterwards, Cancel would leave a running process with no window to get back into. The dialog offers "Don't show this reminder again"; ticking it stops the question, and "Confirm before closing" in Settings brings it back.

callout.title: macOS works differently
callout.text: On macOS, closing a window does not quit the app — it stays in the Dock — so there is no such question there; the confirmation appears on ⌘Q instead, with the window still on screen. One thing to watch on Windows and Linux: the guard is attached to every window, not just the main one, so a Plans or Git window you left open counts as the last one.

s4.p3: Menu items with accelerators follow the platform: ⌘ on macOS, Ctrl on Windows and Linux. Every rule at the pane and editor level can be rebound one by one in Settings ▸ Shortcuts, so if a combination is awkward on your keyboard, change it there.
s4.p4: While a CLI has mouse reporting on, a plain drag is forwarded to the program and selects nothing. Hold <kbd class="cph-kbd">Option</kbd> on macOS, or <kbd class="cph-kbd">Shift</kbd> on Windows and Linux, to force a text selection.

s5.title: What the machinery underneath means for you
s5.p1: Panes on Windows run on the system's ConPTY, which needs a console host executable that the packaging tools do not find on their own. Navide therefore collects it into the bundle explicitly — and every release opens a real ConPTY inside the packaged executable and fails the build if it cannot. Without that file the failure is not occasional: every pane dies the instant it opens. The x64 and Arm64 builds are each checked separately.
s5.p2: CLI panes on Windows receive their command directly, not through PowerShell. PowerShell's -Command re-parses the string as PowerShell code: the braces of the MCP configuration JSON are read as a script block and an & in a URL as the call operator, so every MCP-wired pane used to die at launch on a parser error. Plain terminal panes — the ones that are not a CLI agent — are unchanged and still go through PowerShell.

macos.means: Reading a credential can raise a macOS permission dialog asking you to Allow it. A Navide Cloud connection that sits there going nowhere is usually that dialog waiting for an answer.

windows.means: The file is tied to your Windows account: no other account on the machine can open it, and copying it to another machine will not work either. Nothing ever prompts during a read or write.

linux.means: File permissions are the only thing protecting it — there is no operating-system vault in the way.

s5.p3: Git account tokens are a separate store, kept through the operating system's keychain with only ciphertext on disk. If this machine cannot reach that keychain, the Add account button disappears, existing accounts become read-only, and the page says outright that encryption is unavailable on this system.
s5.p4: On Windows every pane's child processes go into a Job Object: closing the pane closes that handle, and the kernel takes the whole process tree with it — even when Navide itself exits abnormally. The price is that Windows offers no graceful termination signal, so a CLI is terminated outright and may not finish writing its transcript.
s5.p5: macOS and Linux are the other way round: a child starts its own session, so nothing takes it down for free. Navide therefore sweeps on shutdown and sweeps again on the next launch for whatever the previous run missed, and shows a leftover-process warning in the status bar so you can decide whether to clear them. On those two platforms the signal is SIGTERM, which gives a CLI the chance to finish its transcript first.
s5.p6: On all three platforms the backend follows the app out: the app tells the backend its own process id at startup, and the backend watches that id and shuts itself down when it disappears.
s5.h4: Whether your CLIs can be found
s5.p7: A program started from Finder or a desktop launcher inherits a PATH that is not the one you see in a terminal — and every coding CLI's installer writes its directory into a shell startup file. So on macOS and Linux, Navide additionally asks a login shell to print its PATH, and falls back to a list of the usual install locations when the shell will not answer. Windows does none of this: its PATH lives in the registry, so the process already has the complete one.
s5.p8: Claude Code hooks on Linux work without curl: when the hook is installed, Navide checks whether the machine has curl and writes the same request with python3 when it does not. Ubuntu Desktop ships without curl, and a hook that fails quietly takes every hook-driven feature down with it.

win.signing: The installer is not code-signed. Every new version is flagged by SmartScreen again, and in-app updates are installed without signature verification for the same reason.
win.symlinks: Per-pane CLI homes and managed skills are built from symbolic links, which Windows does not let an ordinary process create. Either turn on Windows Developer Mode (Settings ▸ For developers) or run Navide elevated. Without it nothing fails silently: the affected pane prints a yellow [mcp] line explaining why once it starts. This only reaches the CLIs whose MCP wiring is a file in their config directory — Antigravity CLI, Grok CLI and Kimi Code.
win.schedule: The Schedule tab lists only Navide's own jobs (Navide Jobs). Navide reads the user crontab and macOS launchd jobs, and Windows has neither; Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) is deliberately not integrated, because Navide never creates OS scheduled jobs and Task Scheduler already manages the machine's. The screen says so rather than showing you an empty list.

linux.deb: The .deb install has no in-app updates — they come through apt. Use the AppImage if you want the app to update itself.
linux.arm64: arm64 is not published. It is built only on a manual build run and does not appear on the release page.
linux.terminal: "Open in terminal" relies on detection. Linux has no single default terminal, so Navide tries $TERMINAL, then xdg-terminal-exec, then a list of the common emulators; when none of them works it reports a failure rather than quietly doing nothing.

common.macPerms: The macOS privacy prompts — Automation, Files and Folders, Full Disk Access — have no equivalent on Windows or Linux. Wherever another topic tells you to grant something in System Settings, that applies to macOS only.

s7.title: One person, several machines
s7.p1: Connecting two machines running different operating systems is not itself a platform matter: signing in to Navide Cloud, pairing, and cross-device messaging work the same way on all three, and are covered in Settings & System. This section only adds what changes when the machines are not the same platform.
s7.p2: In Settings ▸ Navide Cloud, the sync list currently lets you turn on four things: prompt skills, MCP, skills and memory. Credentials is listed too, but its switch is disabled and its description says syncing is not supported yet — it is there so you know the scope exists, not so you can turn it on.
s7.note: Things that never travel with you anyway: each CLI's own installation and sign-in, credentials (held in each platform's own vault, in formats that do not interchange), and every absolute path. A second machine needs its CLIs installed and signed in on its own.

controls.caption: The same title bar on either side. Drawn in HTML, so it follows your theme.

mac.label: macOS
mac.text: The system paints the traffic lights at the top left, so the title bar reserves a strip on that side for them.

drawn.label: Windows and Linux
drawn.text: Nothing is reserved on the left. Instead Navide draws its own three buttons at the top right: minimize, maximize/restore and close.

mcp.conflict: This file changed outside Agent-Team. Reload before saving again.
mcp.custom-hint: Choose a transport now, then fill in its connection details from the installed-server list.
mcp.external-access-hint: Let an external MCP client connect to Navide over a local HTTP endpoint.
mcp.allow-external-warning: Anything running on this machine can control Navide while this is on.
mcp.cdp-hint: Requires an app restart to take effect. Binds to 127.0.0.1 only.
mcp.cdp-warning: Anything running on this machine can execute arbitrary code in Navide while this is on.
mcp.agent-intro: Servers this machine already has, whoever set them up: Navide's own and the ones each CLI keeps in its own config. Native configs are read only — Navide never edits them.
mcp.agent-empty-body: Nothing is configured for Navide or for any installed CLI.
mcp.agent-error-load: Could not read the MCP configuration.
mcp.filter-label: Filter by where the server is configured
mcp.matrix-hint-disabled: {name} is configured in {agent} but switched off
mcp.matrix-hint-off: {name} is not in {agent}'s user-level config (project-level config is not scanned)
mcp.native-readonly-hint: Navide reads these files and never writes to them. Only each CLI's user-level config is scanned — project-level MCP is not shown. Change a server where its CLI expects it, then refresh.
mcp.navide-scope-hint: Navide connects to this server itself. CLI panes do not receive it.
mcp.catalog-context7: Look up version-correct framework docs (Vue, React, FastAPI…) and inject them into the kickoff so the agent does not hallucinate an old API. Enabled by default.
mcp.catalog-github: Read issues, PRs and commits so the orchestrator can inject the requirement or task background into the pipeline.
mcp.catalog-filesystem: Read the workspace's existing code, README and config files so the orchestrator can inject the current state into the kickoff and correct the agent's starting assumptions.
mcp.catalog-brave-search: Live web search, so the orchestrator can look up the latest technical decisions or API changes and inject them into the agent. Needs a Brave API key.
mcp.catalog-sentry: Read production errors and stack traces so the orchestrator can inject the bug background into the debug stage.
mcp.catalog-hint: This catalog lists only "Orchestrator context-reading" MCPs — tools that read workspace / docs / external service data and inject it into kickoff prompts to ground agent knowledge. Execution actions (tests, browser automation, etc.) are handled by the CLI agents themselves.

credentials.title: Credentials & keys
credentials.intro: A read-only scan of where credentials and keys live on this machine. Nothing is changed, moved or sent anywhere.
credentials.meta: Local only · values never shown · sync off
credentials.keyring-bad-hint: Without a system keyring, credentials tend to end up in plain files.
credentials.incomplete: This scan is incomplete: it hit a time or folder limit, or skipped a repository it could not read safely, so findings in the folders below may be missing.
credentials.banner-high: {count} high-risk finding needs attention | {count} high-risk findings need attention
credentials.banner-high-hint: Open a card for plain advice. Nothing here changes anything for you.
credentials.empty-findings-body: Nothing risky matched the current filter.
credentials.empty-inventory-body: No credentials matched the current filter.
credentials.not-scanned: Press Scan to look for credentials on this machine.

drawer.steps-note: Copy only. Navide never runs these for you.
drawer.manual-fix: This value contains shell characters, so no command is offered. Fix it by hand in the config file shown above.
drawer.no-reveal: Values are never shown here, and there is no reveal button. To see a value, open your system keychain app.

roots.title: Scan roots
roots.intro: Folders searched for git repositories. Workspace roots come from your open workspaces; add more if you keep repos elsewhere.
roots.error: Could not save the scan roots.
roots.error-load: Could not load the scan roots.

code-unknown.title: Credential finding
code-unknown.body: This finding type is not described in this version.

url-token.title: Token embedded in a remote URL
url-token.body: Anyone who can read the repo config, a shell history or a log can see the token. Revoke the token at the provider first, then remove it from the remote URL so git uses the keychain.

ssh-no-passphrase-default-host.title: Default SSH key has no passphrase
ssh-no-passphrase-default-host.body: This key is used for a host by default and anyone who copies the file can use it. Add a passphrase (ssh-keygen -p) and load it into the ssh-agent or keychain.

ssh-no-passphrase.title: SSH key has no passphrase
ssh-no-passphrase.body: Anyone who copies this private key file can use it. Add a passphrase with ssh-keygen -p, or delete the key if you no longer use it.

ssh-key-unreferenced.title: SSH key not referenced anywhere
ssh-key-unreferenced.body: No ssh config entry or known host points at this key, so it may be left over. If you no longer need it, remove it from the provider account and delete the file.

ssh-key-mode.title: SSH key file is readable by others
ssh-key-mode.body: Other users on this machine can read the private key. Run chmod 600 on the file so only you can access it.

cli-token-plaintext.title: CLI token stored in a plain file
cli-token-plaintext.body: The CLI keeps its login token in a readable file instead of the keychain. Log out and back in with the keychain option if the CLI has one, or restrict the file to your user.

gh-active-account-only.title: Only the active gh account is usable
gh-active-account-only.body: The GitHub CLI serves one active account at a time, so repos tied to another account silently use the wrong identity. Run gh auth switch before pushing, or give each repo its own credential helper.

helper-duplicate.title: Duplicate git credential helpers
helper-duplicate.body: The same helper is configured more than once, so git may prompt or store a credential twice. Remove the extra credential.helper lines from your git config.

helper-shadowed.title: A git credential helper is never reached
helper-shadowed.body: An earlier helper answers first, so this one is never used. Check the order of credential.helper entries and keep only the one you want.

env-token-in-shell-rc.title: Token exported in a shell startup file
env-token-in-shell-rc.body: Every program you start inherits this token, and the file is easy to leak or commit. Revoke it at the provider, remove the export line, and load the secret from the keychain when needed.

env-token-set.title: Token set in the environment
env-token-set.body: A credential is present in this app's environment and is passed to every child process. Unset it where it is defined if you do not need it everywhere.

plaintext-credential-file.title: Credentials in a plain file
plaintext-credential-file.body: A file on disk holds credentials in readable text. Move them into the system keychain, restrict the file to your user, and rotate the credential if the file was ever shared or backed up.

keyring-unavailable.title: No system keyring available
keyring-unavailable.body: Without a keyring, tools fall back to plain files. Install and unlock one (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or a Secret Service such as GNOME Keyring) and sign in again.

skills.title: Managed Skills
skills.intro: One place to see every skill your CLIs have, decide who receives which, and create new ones in ~/.agents/skills. A skill in a CLI's own folder moves only when you choose “Move into shared library”, which leaves a link in its old place; “Restore” moves it back.
skills.empty-body: Create a skill in ~/.agents/skills, or install one into any of your CLIs.
skills.sync-too-large-hint: This skill's files are too large to sync between devices. Its on/off and delivery settings still sync.
skills.sync-via-blobs-hint: This skill is too large for one sync record, so its files travel between your devices as encrypted file uploads. Its on/off and delivery settings sync as usual.
skills.editor-hint: Known fields are editable. Other frontmatter values are preserved.
skills.name: Name
skills.user-invocable-hint: Allow users to invoke this skill directly.
skills.model-invocation-hint: Allow the model to select this skill automatically.
skills.attachments-hint: Attachments are read-only here. Open the folder to manage them.
skills.delete-confirm: Move {name} to Trash? You can recover it from the system Trash.
skills.conflict-body: Reload the current file before saving again. Your unsaved draft remains visible until you reload.
skills.error-load: Could not load managed skills. Refresh to try again.
skills.error-load-one: Could not load this skill. Refresh the library and try again.
skills.error-invalid-response: The backend returned an invalid skill record. Refresh to try again.
skills.error-create: Could not create the skill. Check the name and try again.
skills.error-save: Could not save the skill. Your draft remains in the editor.
skills.error-toggle: Could not update the enabled state. Try again.
skills.error-delete: Could not move the skill to Trash. Nothing was deleted.
skills.matrix-planned-hint: {agent} has skills, but Navide does not deliver to it yet.
skills.error-targets: Could not change the delivery targets.
skills.matrix-auto-shared-hint: {agent} reads ~/.agents/skills on its own; nothing to deliver.
skills.matrix-auto-native-hint: {agent} owns this skill and reads it directly.
skills.editor-readonly-hint: This skill is yours, not Navide's — edit it where it lives.
skills.consent-body:
Navide will create this skill inside your own folder:

{root}

Six CLIs (codex, copilot, grok, opencode, muse, cursor) already read that folder, so the skill reaches them immediately. Navide will only ever edit or delete skills it created there — anything else in the folder stays yours and untouched.

You will not be asked again. Continue?
skills.migrate-hint: Move this skill into ~/.agents/skills, leaving a link where it was
skills.migrate-body:
Move “{name}” into Navide's shared library?

1. It will be moved from
   {from}
   into
   {root}

2. A link will be left in its old place, so {agent} keeps reading it exactly as before.

3. You can undo this at any time with “Restore” — it moves back and the link goes away.

Nothing else in either folder is touched. Continue?
skills.error-migrate: Could not move the skill. Nothing was changed.
skills.error-restore: Could not restore the skill. Nothing was changed.
skills.delivery-hint: ● reads it on its own · ✓ delivered by Navide (click to toggle) · greyed: not delivered
skills.enabled-hint: Off means Navide delivers it nowhere; CLIs that read it on their own still see it.
skills.native-conflict-hint: A CLI's own skill has this name and wins for that CLI.

inventory.title: This machine and the cloud
inventory.hint: How many items each synced section holds here and in the cloud.
inventory.no-writes: Nothing written to the cloud yet
inventory.notice-no-key: This device does not hold the account's sync key yet, so the cloud is closed to it. Pair it with a device that holds the key and the numbers appear here.
inventory.notice-not-connected: Sign in to Navide Cloud to compare this machine with the cloud.
inventory.notice-error: The cloud could not be read.
inventory.row-error: Could not read this section from the cloud.
inventory.row-no-key: This device has no sync key yet.

devices.title: Devices that wrote to the cloud
devices.hint: Every device that has written a record to this account.
devices.none: No device has written to the cloud yet.
devices.partial: Some sections could not be read, so this list may be incomplete.

share.title: Share links
share.hint: Read-only links to a plan or report, encrypted on this machine. The key travels only inside the link; the server stores ciphertext it cannot open.
share.unavailable: Share links are not available in this version yet.
share.error: Share links could not be loaded.
share.rekeyed: New link copied; the old one no longer opens.
share.rekeyed-old-alive: New link copied. The server did not confirm the old link stopped; revoke it if it must not open.

sync.title: Sync
sync.hint: Turn on a section to keep it the same on every device signed in to this account. Records are encrypted on this machine; the server stores ciphertext it has no key for.
sync.retired-memory: Memory is not synced any more. Switch it off; your instruction files here and the copies in the cloud are left as they are.
sync.not-connected: Not connected — synced sections catch up when the link is back.
sync.no-key: This device has no sync key yet; nothing is uploaded until it has one.
sync.conflicts-hint: Two devices changed the same item. Nothing was overwritten — pick which one to keep.
sync.approvals-hint: Another device sent something that would run here. Nothing is written, enabled or sent to a CLI until you approve it.
sync.approval-undisplayable: This record cannot be displayed in full here, so it cannot be approved. Reject it.
sync.approval-cut: … preview cut here; the file goes on
sync.approval-frontmatter: SKILL.md frontmatter (the CLIs act on it)
sync.approval-frontmatter-flag: {key}: makes a CLI run something or allow more — check it
sync.approval-turn-on: Would switch this skill on: it is off here.
sync.approvals-full: Too many records are waiting in {scopes}: new ones are refused until you decide some.
sync.secret-warnings-hint: These items read like they hold a key or token. They still sync, encrypted; check them, then dismiss.
sync.scope-hint-prompts: Prompt skills and the loop prompt.
sync.error-load: Sync settings could not be read.
sync.scope-hint-mcp: MCP servers you added in Navide. Their secrets are encrypted before they leave.
sync.scope-hint-skills: Which skills are on and which CLIs each one goes to, plus the files of skills created in Navide (large ones travel as encrypted blobs). Skills you put in the folder yourself sync their settings only.
sync.scope-hint-memory: Global instruction files such as ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Files inside a project stay with git.
sync.scope-hint-credentials: Portable CLI credentials you pasted in Accounts. Encrypted on this device before they leave; removing one here never removes it from the cloud or your other devices.
sync.rotate-hint: Rotating retires the current key: every synced record is re-sealed under a new one and your other devices receive it the next time they exchange keys. Use it if you suspect the key leaked.
sync.legacy-key: A sync key from before accounts were bound is on this device. Adopt it for this account to keep reading what was synced with it.
sync.skipped-no-key: Skipped — this device has no sync key.
sync.skipped-unsupported: Skipped — the server cannot store this section's files.
sync.result-refused: Could not be applied on this device: {items}
sync.result-reset-throttled: The server's state looks wrong, so re-syncing this section is paused; it retries in an hour.
sync.secrets-title: Hidden values — keeping a side changes the ones that differ:
sync.history-hint: The cloud keeps each synced item's last 10 versions or 30 days of them, whichever ends first.
sync.history-no-items: Nothing in this section is synced yet.
sync.history-empty: No earlier versions of this item.
sync.history-restored: Restored here. It reaches your other devices on the next sync.
sync.history-held: The restored version is waiting for your approval above.
sync.history-error: Version history could not be loaded.
sync.history-not-applied: Nothing changed here: this version was not applied (it may have been declined before).

sharing.intro: Two ways to move these four sections between machines: a file you hand over, and the account they already share.

bundle.title: Settings bundle
bundle.intro: Pack Prompts, MCP servers, Skills and instruction files into one file somebody else can open. Secret values are left out of it; whoever imports it fills them in. This half needs no account and no connection.
bundle.secrets-hint: Its env and header values are emptied on the way out; whoever imports it has to fill them in.
bundle.may-leak-hint: Its args or url look like they contain a token. That is NOT stripped — it goes out exactly as written. Check it before ticking this item.
bundle.description-placeholder: What is in here, and who it is for
bundle.export-empty: Tick at least one item before exporting.
bundle.error-load: The shareable items could not be listed.
bundle.error-export: The bundle could not be written.
bundle.error-read-file: That file could not be read.
bundle.error-not-a-bundle: That file is not a settings bundle: it is not valid JSON.
bundle.error-preview: That bundle could not be read.
bundle.error-apply: The import could not be applied.
bundle.preview-intro: Nothing has been changed yet. This bundle carries {count} item(s) — tick the ones to apply.
bundle.needs-credentials-hint: Its secret values were left out of the bundle: {fields}. They keep this machine's values only if the server runs the same command or URL as this machine's; otherwise they stay empty and must be filled in.

cloud.title: What is in the cloud
cloud.intro: This machine and the account, side by side. Bodies never leave: items are compared by fingerprint, so the list can say whether two copies match without either of them being shown.
cloud.unreadable-hint: A row marked "Cannot be read" was written by another device under a different key, so this machine cannot open it. Pushing or pulling will not settle it — sign in on the device that wrote it, or remove the cloud copy from there.
cloud.notice-not-connected: Not signed in to Navide Cloud, or the link is down — so there is nothing to compare against yet.
cloud.notice-no-key: This device does not hold the account's sync key yet, so cloud records stay closed to it. Pair it with a device that already has the key.
cloud.notice-error: This section's cloud listing could not be read.
cloud.notice-unknown-scope: This build does not know this section, so the cloud holds nothing for it.
cloud.notice-disabled: Sync is off for this section, so nothing moves on its own. The listing is here so you can see what turning it on would bring.
cloud.notice-empty: Neither this device nor the cloud holds anything in this section.
cloud.offline-pointer: The settings bundle above works offline: export a file and carry it across by hand.
cloud.devices-title: Devices that wrote to the cloud
cloud.devices-hint: Two times, kept apart: when the device last wrote a record to this account, and when the server last saw it online. A device the server has not named is listed by the start of its id.
cloud.no-devices: No device has written anything to this account yet.
cloud.error-load: The cloud listing could not be read.
cloud.error-move: Those items could not be moved.

memory.title: CLI Instruction Files
memory.intro: Every CLI reads an instruction file before it starts working — CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, QWEN.md, .cursor rules. Each file is listed once, with every CLI that loads it, and can be edited in place.
memory.no-workspace: No folder is open, so only user-level files are listed.
memory.create-hint: This file does not exist yet. Saving creates it, and any missing folder above it.
memory.conflict-body: Another program — a CLI or an editor — changed this file while you were editing it. Saving now would overwrite that change.
memory.agents-mapped-hint: Navide knows where these CLIs keep their instructions.
memory.agents-configured-hint: These CLIs have no instruction file name of their own: name the files under the `read:` key of .aider.conf.yml, and the ones you name appear in the list above.
memory.agents-unknown-hint: Navide has no instruction file path for these CLIs.
memory.error-load: Could not list the instruction files. Refresh to try again.
memory.error-save: Could not save this file. Your draft remains in the editor.

prompts.title: Prompt Skills
prompts.intro: Reusable whole instructions a CLI pane can cast from its ∞ button. One skill is one complete prompt — picking a skill replaces the prompt, it never appends to another. Only the default skill runs as a loop; every other skill is sent once.
prompts.name: Name
prompts.icon-custom-hint: Type or paste any emoji to use it as this skill's icon.
prompts.resume-placeholder: Leave empty to use the global resume text
prompts.hint: The default skill is what a plain click on ∞ casts, and the only one that loops; disabled skills stay here but leave the picker.
prompts.send-once-hint: Only the default skill runs as a loop; this one is sent once, with no resume or turn cap.

p2p.title: Connection
p2p.hint: Navide Cloud links your devices into one private network, so agents here can message agents anywhere you are signed in.
p2p.token-placeholder: Paste the token issued by your server
p2p.token-hint: Kept in the system keychain and never shown again.
p2p.link-connecting: Connecting to the server. These become available in a moment.
p2p.err-timeout: The server did not answer in time.
p2p.err-dns: The server address could not be resolved.
p2p.err-tls: The secure connection could not be established.
p2p.err-reset: The other end closed the connection.
p2p.link-waiting-keychain: Waiting for Keychain access. Look for a macOS dialog and allow it — no dial has been made.
p2p.link-not-connected: Not connected to the server, so nothing here can be changed right now.

pair.compare: Check that {device} is showing these same six digits.
pair.err-generic: That answer did not go through.
pair.hint: Different digits on the two screens means something is in between. Refuse, and nothing pairs.
pair.later-title: Hides this request. It comes back if that device asks again.
pair.salvaged: {device} was recovered from a damaged pairing record. Its key is kept, but it needs your approval again
pair.sig2-missing: {device} sent a message without its time signature — a server that does not pass it on, or something on the way removed it. It was delivered
pair.sig2-unusable: {device} sent a message whose time signature did not check out, or was dated too far from this machine's clock. It was delivered on the older signature; check both machines' clocks
pair.sig2-refused-missing: {device} sent a message without its time signature, and it was refused: that device signs one, so something on the way removed it
pair.sig2-refused-unusable: {device} sent a message whose time signature did not check out, and it was refused
pair.sig2-refused-clock-ahead: A message from {device} was refused for clock skew: that machine's clock is {minutes} minutes ahead of this one. Check both machines' clocks
pair.sig2-refused-clock-behind: A message from {device} was refused for clock skew: that machine's clock is {minutes} minutes behind this one, or the message was held back on the way. Check both machines' clocks
pair.full: Pairing limit reached: {device} could not be paired. Update Navide to add more devices.
pair.start-title: Ask to pair with this device. Both screens show six digits to compare, and nothing changes until both sides confirm.
pair.title: Pairing
pair.waiting-remote: You confirmed. Waiting for the other device.
pair.waiting-response: Sent. It comes up on that device’s screen — there is nothing to open there.
pair.your-turn: The digits are on both screens. Nothing is paired until you say they match.
pair.dismiss-title: Hides this notice. The request keeps running, and the answer will appear here.
pair.failed-local-trust-unavailable: {device} answered, but this machine cannot read its trust record right now, so the answer was refused and this pairing has ended. Deal with the “Navide Cloud is stopped” card below first (for example, press “Start over”), then press “Pair” again.
pair.failed-local-pairing-refused: The answer from {device} did not fit this pairing, so it was ended to be safe. Press “Pair” to try again.
pair.failed-local-other: This machine could not accept the answer from {device} ({reason}), so this pairing has ended. Press “Pair” to try again.
pair.failed-remote-trust-unavailable: {device} cannot read its trust record right now, so it refused this pairing and the pairing has ended. On {device}, deal with the “Navide Cloud is stopped” card in the account window (for example, press “Start over”), then press “Pair” again.
pair.failed-remote-policy-denied: {device} refused this pairing, so it has ended. This machine may be on the block list on {device}; check there in the account window, then press “Pair” again.
pair.failed-remote-unauthenticated: {device} could not verify this pairing’s signature, so it refused it and the pairing has ended. Make sure both machines run the latest Navide, then press “Pair” again.
pair.failed-remote-pairing-refused: {device} refused this pairing, so it has ended. Usually {device} already has a pairing in progress (for example, both sides pressed “Pair” at once). Wait for it to finish or cancel it on {device}, then press “Pair” again.
pair.failed-remote-other: {device} refused this pairing ({reason}), so it has ended. Press “Pair” to try again.
pair.busy: A pairing with {device} is still in progress and ends by itself in about {minutes} min. To start over now, press “Cancel request” in the Pairing section above, then press “Pair” again.
pair.trust-unavailable-start: This machine cannot read its trust record right now, so pairing cannot succeed. Deal with the “Navide Cloud is stopped” card below first (for example, press “Start over”), then press “Pair”.

p2p.token-only-note: Signing in with an account is what shows your other devices and lets you pair with them.
p2p.first-pair-1: Sign in to this account on the other device.
p2p.first-pair-2: Open the account window there and here.
p2p.first-pair-3: Press Pair, then check both screens show the same six digits.

policy.title: Who may command panes on this device
policy.hint: Applies only to messages arriving from other devices. Agents on this one are unaffected.
policy.default-deny: Nothing is allowed by default: a message is refused unless a rule below matches it.
policy.readonly-short: These rules can only be changed while connected.
policy.readonly: These rules live on the server, so they change only while connected. This is the last set received.
policy.resign-hint: Only needed when a "rules could not be verified" warning is showing.
policy.resigned: Rules signed with this device's key.
policy.own-devices-hint: Any device signed in to this account may message any pane here, including ones added later.
policy.empty: No rules — every message from another device is refused.

account.account-hint: An account gives you a private network: only devices signed in to it can see each other.
account.hint-titlebar: Sign in, paste a token or sign out from the account button in the titlebar.
account.open-window: Sign in or create an account…
account.verify-sent: We sent a verification link to {email}. Open it to confirm this address.
account.verify-still-pending: Still not confirmed. If you just clicked the link, give it a moment — this updates on its own.
account.not-verified-next: Check your mail for the link.
account.verify-resent: Sent. Check your inbox — the link is good for 24 hours.
account.verify-rate-limited: A link was just sent. Wait a minute before asking for another.
account.verify-required: Verify your email address before inviting people.

network.title: Your network
network.loading: Asking the server who is signed in…
network.unavailable: This device is not linked to a network yet.
network.last-seen-unknown: Not seen since this device started
network.solo: Only this device is signed in. Sign in on another device to see it here.
network.link-offline: The link is down, so this is the last thing the server said.
network.not-current: This may not be current — the last read did not come back.
network.git-never-fetched: Never fetched — ahead/behind may be out of date

trust.requests-hint: Approving writes a rule for exactly this pane. Nothing else on this device is granted.
trust.blocked-hint: A block is refused ahead of every rule, including your own other devices.
trust.block-full: This machine's pairing record is full, so the block could not be saved. Unpair this device first, then block it.
trust.block-not-saved-full: Blocked on the server, but this machine's pairing record is full, so it did not save its own copy. This machine still refuses the device until it restarts. To save the copy, unpair this device, then block it again.
trust.block-not-saved: Blocked on the server, but this machine did not save its own copy. This machine still refuses the device until it restarts. Block it again later so this machine keeps a copy.
trust.unpair-title: Forget this device. It is not blocked.
trust.first-seen-own-body: It claims to be yours, which would skip your rules — so it is held until you confirm it.
trust.pending-body: Confirm each device by matching the fingerprint shown on that device.
trust.pending-later-title: Off the list without deciding. Returns on the next attempt.
trust.key-changed-body: Its messages are refused. It may have been reinstalled, or somebody may be standing in for it.
trust.key-changed-what-to-do: Compare these two with that device's owner first. There is deliberately no button here.
trust.policy-unverified: Your rules could not be verified
trust.policy-unverified-body: Nothing is accepted from other devices until they verify. Open the rules and sign them again.
trust.policy-sign-when: Only needed when this warning is showing.
trust.policy-signed-default: There were no rules to re-sign, so the default was signed: nothing is allowed yet.
trust.locked-body: This device had trust state and no longer does. Nothing is sent or accepted until that is clear.
trust.full-body: The trust record is full. Unpair a device below to make room; Navide Cloud reconnects on its own once there is.
trust.damaged-body: The pairing record is damaged — pair again. The record on this machine was saved incomplete (a Keychain write was cut off), so nothing in it can be trusted.
trust.journal-problem: The pairing notice record cannot be used right now. Pairing itself is unaffected, but notices and the record of messages already received may be incomplete for now. Reason:
trust.damaged-rebuild-warn: This erases the damaged pairing record on this machine. Each of your other devices must then be paired again, from both ends. The record is already damaged, so starting over is the fix.
trust.plaintext-refused-body: This device has always sent encrypted messages; this one arrived in the clear, so it was refused.
trust.plaintext-refused-what-to-do: Nothing to do — it was refused. If that device is legitimate, unpair it and pair again.
trust.member-changed: {device} now answers to a different account
trust.member-changed-body: Same pinned key, so the same device — but the server now says it belongs to a different account.
trust.unknown-notice: Security notice this version cannot display ({kind})
trust.rebuild-title: Clear this machine’s trust record and start again. Every pairing is lost.
trust.rebuild-warn: This erases every pairing on this machine. Each of your other devices must be paired again, from both ends. Do this only if you know why the record cannot be read — if you do not, it is worth finding out first.
trust.rebuild-done: The trust record was cleared. Pair your devices again when you are ready.
trust.locked-retrying: This may be temporary — a locked keychain or a dismissed permission dialog reads the same way from here. It is still being retried; if it clears, nothing was lost.

link.paused-body: This device is not talking to the network. Your account and settings are kept.

cliAgents.title: CLI Agents
cliAgents.hint: Enable and reorder the CLI agents in the manual spawn dropdown. Open a card to manage that agent. At least one must stay enabled.
cliAgents.reorder-filtered: Clear search and choose All to reorder
cliAgents.overview-hint: Choose a tab to adjust this agent. Changes save automatically. Launch settings apply to newly started panes.
cliAgents.no-push-channel: This agent does not declare a push channel. Messages use the normal terminal input path.

cliLaunch.title: Launch overrides
cliLaunch.hint: Set this CLI's default model and effort, replace its launch command, or add environment variables. These per-CLI settings apply to newly started panes in every window.
cliLaunch.no-model-args: This CLI cannot be told which model to run at launch, so there is nothing to choose — switch model inside the CLI instead.
cliLaunch.command-placeholder: Leave empty to use the default
cliLaunch.command-shadows-model: A launch command means you are writing the whole line, so Navide stops adding to it: the model and effort above, the permission-bypass flag and any per-pane argument are all left off. Clear this field to get them back.
cliLaunch.command-shadows-resume: It also applies to a FRESH pane only. Rebuilding a pane, or restoring one after a restart, has to rebuild the resume command from the vendor's own syntax — so those panes launch on the default command, not this one. Navide cannot merge the two: it has no way to know where an id belongs inside a line you wrote.
cliLaunch.env-reserved-warn: Navide manages this variable itself, so a value set here never reaches the CLI. You can still save it — it starts working the day Navide stops managing it.
cliLaunch.reserved-note: Variables Navide manages itself and will not pass through: {list}
cliLaunch.restart-note: All of this is fixed into a pane when it starts. Changing anything here affects panes spawned afterwards; a pane already running keeps what it started with until it is rebuilt or restored.

cli.title: CLI Accounts
cli.hint: Click "Sign in" or "+ New account" to open a temporary login pane; it closes once you authorize in the browser. "Set as default" picks the account new panes use, and open panes keep theirs until reopened.
cli.hint-detail: All accounts share your home directory, so sessions and history carry over; switching swaps the stored credentials in place, and signing in never touches the active account.

cli.agent-login-confirm-title: An agent asks to open a CLI sign-in
cli.agent-login-confirm-body: Nothing opens unless you agree. The sign-in pane runs the CLI's own login and you finish it in the browser; the agent sees none of it. If you do not answer, the request closes by itself.
cli.agent-login-confirm-reason-truncated: The agent's reason was longer than 300 characters; only the first 300 are shown.
cli.agent-switch-confirm-title: An agent asks to switch a CLI account
cli.agent-switch-confirm-body: Nothing switches unless you agree. The switch is the same one Settings → Accounts makes: the CLI moves to the other account, and if panes are running on it Navide asks you again before restarting them. If you do not answer, the request closes by itself.
cli.agent-switch-confirm-late: Once you agree, the switch finishes even if the agent has stopped waiting. If panes are restarted, that includes the asking agent's own pane when it runs on this CLI; it will not get the result and has to check its accounts again after the restart.

cli.global-login-body: {agent} has no isolated sign-in. During sign-in its live credential is temporarily replaced by the new account; when the sign-in completes the current account ({current}) is restored, and the new account is used only when you switch to it. Running {agent} panes block this — close or finish them first.

pushChannels.title: Push channels
pushChannels.hint: Some CLIs can be handed a message directly instead of having it typed into the pane. This is per CLI; switching one off means every message to those panes is typed in, exactly as it was before. A pane already running keeps its channel until it is restarted, but nothing is pushed to it any more.
pushChannels.restart-note: Claude's channel is a hook in its settings file. Switching it either way rewrites ~/.claude/settings.json straight away, but a Claude pane already open started with the old file and only picks the change up the next time it starts.
pushChannels.cost-opencode: Opens a local port with no password — anything running as you can drive the pane. The message still goes into the input box.
pushChannels.cost-kilo: Opens a local port protected by a per-pane password. The message still goes into the input box.
pushChannels.cost-qwen: Keeps a per-pane file in Navide's data directory; each message is written to it in the clear until the pane closes. Never touches the input box.
pushChannels.cost-claude: Installs a background hook that waits on Navide, so an idle agent can be woken. Never touches the input box.
pushChannels.all-off-title: All channels off — messages still arrive, by a different route
pushChannels.all-off-delivery: A message now waits for the receiving pane to go idle and is then typed into it, so it takes longer to land.
pushChannels.all-off-rewake: Claude Code's rewake is the only way to wake an idle agent; with it off, there is nothing to do but wait for the agent to come back to idle on its own.
pushChannels.all-off-restart: A pane already running keeps the channel it started with until it is restarted.

hint.stall-strict: Strict mode: no sentinel or completion intent detected. Keep waiting resets the idle timer; Force advance marks this slot done.
